# Independent audit: all-dimensional finite near-simplex cap stability

Audited source: all-dimensional-near-simplex-cap-stability-root.md.

uniform local ordinary stability theorem in each fixed dimension,
not a fixed-roof asymptotic and not an OC conclusion.

The audit independently checked all sections, with particular attention
to the exact radial measure, arbitrary normals, the actual candidate,
and the use of minimum enclosing simplices. The source was read in
full, together with its quantitative facet-functional proof, the
constructive critical vertex-averaging dependency, the archived exact
local simplex cap formula, and the minimum-simplex theorem.

## 1. The facet-functional input has the stated sign and constant

For the facet with d coordinates, the density of the vertex-averaging
law at b=1/(d+1) is N/[d(1-b)^(d-1)]. The denominator is precisely
(d+1)Gamma_d. Applying the quantitative concave inequality to -f,
with f>=0 convex and f(g_F)=0, gives

    integral N f <=(d+1)Gamma_d(1-c_d) integral f.

The sign is correct, and no upper bound on sup f/integral f is
required. The constant is exactly
[1-d^(1-d)]/[(d-1)^2(d+1)], which is positive and less than one
for every d>=2. I checked the supplying proof's minimum-coordinate
conditioning, monotone likelihood ratio, and covariance step: they
apply to all continuous convex f vanishing at the facet centroid,
including profiles concentrating towards boundary faces. They do not
use the stability theorem being audited.

The simplex centroid equality-normal classification used later is
the standard ordinary single-cap equality input recorded in
continuous-minimum-maximal-depth-simplex-rigidity.md. The exact local
vertex-cap formula and its compact-normal consequence are proved in
the stated truncation note. Neither is a mixed-integer assumption.

## 2. The uniform strip estimate is relative, not additive

Conditional averaging of f at a fixed barycentric coordinate t gives
a nonnegative convex function A(t), since the point (t,(1-t)w)
depends affinely on t for every fixed w. Applying Jensen on a
symmetric interval and bounding the conditional density below gives
the ratio [(1-t)/(1-t-r)]^(k-1). The chosen r makes this ratio
less than two, including the k=1 case. Thus the strip estimate is
valid with C=8(d+1) on the relevant facets.

The facet opposite the tested barycentric coordinate has that
coordinate identically zero. Its contribution to the specified
strip is exactly zero, since the strip width is at most b/4<b.
This handles the only constant-coordinate degeneracy.

## 3. Gauge convexity and the exact radial measure

The inner simplex makes g_S an actual interior point of K, so its
gauge is finite and continuous. Restricting the convex gauge to a
facet is a restriction to an affine set; subtracting one preserves
convexity. Because K subset S, a point on the S boundary has gauge
at least one. Facet-centroid membership in K forces equality there.
Hence every f_j=rho-1 meets the functional input exactly.

The quotient identity

    [1-rho^(-d)]/(rho-1)=sum_(a=1)^d rho^(-a)

proves both inequalities in (10), including rho=1 by continuity.
The lower factor is d(1-delta)^d, not a first-order approximation.

The centroid pyramids have equal volume |S|/(d+1), and their
radial Jacobian is d r^(d-1). Their boundaries overlap only on
null sets. Thus tau and the canonical losses have the exact
disintegrations in (11)-(12). Canonical cap membership along a
ray is constant because
lambda_i(g+r(z-g))-b=r(lambda_i(z)-b). All boundary hyperplanes
have zero ordinary volume. The conversion from f_j back to missing
volume has exactly the factor (1-delta)^(-d) claimed in (12).

## 4. Moving normals and thresholds are controlled simultaneously

If a missing point enters a nearby cap but is outside its canonical
cap, its barycentric margin is within eta of zero. Its radial
coordinate is at least 1-delta, so its facet endpoint lies in the
strip of width eta/(1-delta). There is NO additive O(delta) shift
of this strip. This exact identity is essential when the missing
mass is much smaller than delta.

Applying the uniform weighted strip bound and the exact gauge
comparison yields (15) with exponent -d-1. All estimates are for
the same actual halfspace, so they do not assume separate choices
of normals on the individual pyramids or facets.

The eta choice precedes the smallness choices for delta and tau.
It makes E<=Gamma*c/4. Also
(1-c)/(1-c/4)<=1-3c/4, so the simultaneous bounds in (17) obey
the sum in (18). Taking the minimum with tau is legitimate because
every loss is at most the entire missing volume. No allocation or
independence of the L_i is assumed.

## 5. All-normal localization and the actual center

For the standard simplex, through-point cap volume is jointly
continuous in the point and unit normal, by dominated convergence
away from the limiting hyperplane. The finitely many minimizing
normals at g are the canonical apex-side ones. One can FIRST
choose disjoint neighborhoods where the specified scaled affine
margin is uniformly eta-close to the canonical margin. The vertex
signs then stay strict because eta<b. The compact complement has
a strictly positive gap rho_0, and shrinking the point neighborhood
preserves half that gap. These constants depend only on the
dimension and previously fixed eta, not on K or its missing set.

The candidate in (19) has barycentric displacement at most
tau/[(d+1)Gamma]. The conditions tau<=Gamma/2 and delta<=1/4
place every coordinate above b/2>delta/(d+1). It is therefore in
the INTERIOR of the actual contained inner simplex and hence of K.
This establishes actual admissibility before any cap estimate.

For a nearby normal, the cap isolates exactly one vertex. The
intercept product and AM-GM yield (20). The degree>=2 product
terms have total absolute value at most (2^d/Gamma)tau^2, since
tau/Gamma<=1. Its linear term cancels the corresponding L_i
exactly, leaving the common bound Gamma-Lbar-B tau^2. All other
normals retain the fixed positive gap after deleting volume tau.
Parallel tightening covers every containing closed halfspace.

The constants in (24) ensure each condition in this chain at once.
In particular the final numerator is at least Gamma*c*tau/4,
and division by 1-tau can only improve that positive lower bound.
Thus the proof constructs one actual point paying every direction;
it does not merely optimize a finite collection of canonical caps.

## 6. The minimum-enclosing-simplex application is valid

The enclosing-simplex dependency proves existence without escaped
vertices, facet-centroid contact by a feasible facet tilt, and
the stated quantitative vertex matching for EVERY minimizer.
The larger constant L=8(d+1)^3 in the audited source dominates
8d^3, while its first epsilon bound is stricter than the dependency's
1/(64d^3). Its centroid estimate follows by averaging matched
vertices, with no additional normal continuity assertion needed.

The infinity ball of radius1/[d(d+1)] about g_T lies in T: each
coordinate remains nonnegative and their sum remains at most one.
This proves the displayed support gap. Applying the Hausdorff
support bounds to S and the centroid bound gives

    h_inner<=h_T-delta_d||u||_1/[d(d+1)]
                                      +L epsilon_d||u||_1.

The second epsilon choice makes this at most h_T-epsilon_d||u||_1,
which is at most h_K. Thus the EXACT inner simplex required in
(5) is contained in K. The facet-centroid contacts are already
actual points of K. The relative theorem therefore applies, and
ordinary affine invariance returns the constructed center and
enclosing simplex to the original frame.

Dimension one is explicitly separated. All uses of radial volume,
hyperplane nullity and affine normalization concern positive full
ordinary d-volume. No intrinsic mixed-fiber invariance is inferred.

## 7. Verification scope

The independent standard-library verifier
supporting computation verify_all_dimensional_near_simplex_stability_helly_audit.py checks
the exact gauge quotient and bounds, strip-ratio constants,
simultaneous-loss budget, balanced candidate expansion and final
normalization, plus the enclosing-simplex locality constants.
These finite arithmetic checks supplement the line audit; the
compact all-normal argument and uniform relative estimate are
proved analytically in the source and checked above.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
